Popper argues that preferring the better-corroborated theory is rational not because it is more probable (induction), but because it has withstood more severe tests, making it the most informative and critically vetted option available. By reducing the choice to a non-rational biological necessity, the target misrepresents Popper's epistemology, which explicitly provides a logical basis for action (choosing the theory that has survived the most rigorous attempts at falsification) without invoking induction or abandoning reason to biology.", "outcome": "raised and not answered; the target's status did not move"}
